text.arabic_uthmani: وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّآ أَن لَّن تَقُولَ ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِبًۭا

words.gloss_range: and, with additive or resumptive force; locally a prefixed connector carrying the jinn testimony forward

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: variant-like recitation surface for the opening connector plus speaker frame

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) begins by making the confession a continuation of the surrounding testimony, so the ayah is heard as another admitted item in the jinn's report rather than as a detached maxim. Its addition does not by itself establish chronology; it lets the correction accumulate. The variant-like vowel pressure in {{ar:وِإِنَّا}} ({{tr:wi-innā}}) can make the transition audible at the recitation surface, but that remains a delivery feature around the connector, not a new route for the clause.

topics.headline: connector resumes confessed testimony
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah as cumulative jinn testimony, with this confession added to the report rather than isolated from it.
topics.reason: QAC treats the word as a prefixed conjunction on the following annā phrase, and the clause evidence frames the whole ayah as continuing the speakers' assertion.

topics.headline: vowel pressure marks transition audibly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can notice that some recitational surface evidence makes the move into the confession sound smoothed, while syntax still rests on the connector.
topics.reason: The cited vowel shift affects phonetic transition into the clause, but QAC and attachment evidence keep the prefixed conjunction as the syntactic function.

words.gloss_range: that we / indeed we depending on reading; locally a framing particle with attached first-person plural subject

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: contrastive reading of the opening as a more direct assertion

words.prose: {{ar:أَنَّا}} ({{tr:annā}}) puts the first-person plural speakers into view before the verb, so the mistaken judgment is owned communally from the start of the clause. That makes the move self-corrective: the speakers are not only accusing another figure from 72:4, but admitting their own prior assumption. The {{ar:وَإِنَّا}} ({{tr:wa-innā}}) reading can make the opening sound more directly assertive, while the local annā framing keeps the admission tied to reported testimony and preserves the same plural confessing voice.

topics.headline: plural speaker owns the mistake
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the confession as communal self-correction before the actual verb of supposing appears.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the attached first-person plural pronoun as the governed subject of the annā frame, continuing the reported speakers.

topics.headline: reading contrast shifts assertion force
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can distinguish a more assertive recitational framing from a more dependent reported-speech framing without changing who confesses.
topics.reason: The reading contrast affects the force of the opening particle, but both analyses preserve the same first-person plural speaker and the same confession.

words.gloss_range: we thought, supposed, deemed, or assumed; locally a completed communal judgment now exposed as mistaken
words.root_gloss_range: supposition, expectation, probability, and sometimes confident belief; locally corrigible judgment rather than certain knowledge

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: embedded negated speech clause governed as the content of supposition
same-surah recurrence of supposition plus future negation at 72:7

words.prose: {{ar:ظَنَنَّآ}} ({{tr:ẓanannā}}) makes the confession a completed past act of judgment: the speakers had treated a future false-speech event as impossible, and now report that assumption as exposed. The verb governs {{ar:أَن لَّن تَقُولَ}} ({{tr:an lan taqūla}}), so the denied speech clause is the content of their cognition rather than a narrator's independent denial. Its root range preserves confident but corrigible supposition, including grounds of expectation and passive supposability, not verified knowledge, and the Form I plural keeps responsibility inside the speakers rather than shifting blame to an outside cause. The same mistaken-certainty shape recurs with {{ar:ظَنُّوا۟ أَن لَّن}} ({{tr:ẓannū an lan}}) in 72:7, 72:12 keeps assumptions about Allah inside the same correction sequence, and 10:36 warns that supposition cannot replace truth.

topics.headline: completed judgment is now confessed
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse reports a prior mental state now corrected, not an assumption still being endorsed.
topics.reason: QAC parses a first-person plural perfect verb, and the root profile supports supposition or deeming without requiring certain knowledge.

topics.headline: supposition contains the negated clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that their mistake was a whole projected proposition: that neither class would say such a falsehood.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the following an-lan clause the clausal complement governed by the verb.

topics.headline: simple Form I keeps blame internal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers confess their own mistaken judgment rather than presenting themselves as caused or trapped by another agent.
topics.reason: The local form is simple Form I perfect, not a causative or intensive/reflexive form.

topics.headline: root field marks probable judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can keep the epistemic register of supposition in view: the word belongs to a family of expectation and deeming, not bare sensory report.
topics.reason: V4 lexical evidence supports the root family around supposition, probability, and things deemed likely.

topics.headline: supposition and future negation recur
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 72:5 as part of a wider epistemic correction, with 72:7 repeating the supposition-plus-future-negation pattern and 10:36 exposing supposition's weakness against truth.
topics.reason: The cited inter-ayah rows give concrete anchors at 72:7, 72:12, and 10:36; these sharpen the local confession without overriding the local parse.

topics.headline: sound thickens the confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may hear the repeated n-sound as an acoustic concentration around the plural confession before the sweeping negation.
topics.reason: The sound observation is locally real at the surface, but it remains phonetic texture rather than a grammatical or lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: that; locally a complementizer packaging the negated speech clause as the content of supposition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: future-negated speech sequence embedded by the complementizer

words.prose: {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) is the hinge that turns the following {{ar:لَّن تَقُولَ}} ({{tr:lan taqūla}}) sequence into what the speakers had believed. It prevents the future negation from floating as narrator comment: the impossibility claim is embedded inside the prior act of supposing.

topics.headline: hinge embeds the negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader tracks the negation as believed content, not as a free-standing denial by the narrator.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this particle introduce the content complement governed by the preceding supposition verb.

words.gloss_range: will not / would never; locally a strong prospective negator governing the following subjunctive speech verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: subjunctive speech verb governed by the negator
preceding complementizer that embeds the negated speech clause

words.prose: {{ar:لَّن}} ({{tr:lan}}) makes the assumed content strongly prospective: the speakers did not merely doubt that false attribution had happened, they supposed it would not happen. Because it governs {{ar:تَقُولَ}} ({{tr:taqūla}}), the negation belongs inside the content clause and shapes the verb's mood. Its placement before the verb lets impossibility be heard before the human and jinn subjects are named, and the tightened contact after {{ar:أَن}} ({{tr:an}}) adds acoustic compression without changing that scope.

topics.headline: strong negation projects impossibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the error as overconfident prediction about future false speech, not merely a mistaken report about the past.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the particle govern the subjunctive speech verb inside the clausal complement of the supposition.

topics.headline: contact tightens the negation onset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader may hear the embedded negation begin with a compact boundary after the complementizer, while its grammatical job remains negation.
topics.reason: The surface assimilation is audible texture at the particle boundary; it does not alter the attachment of negation to the following verb.

words.gloss_range: say, speak, or assert; locally a subjunctive imperfect speech verb under future negation with explicit content and attribution frame
words.root_gloss_range: saying, formulated assertion, public report, doctrine, and attributed speech; locally accountable assertion rather than mere sound

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: future negator governing the local speech verb
coordinated visible-hidden class subject of the speech verb
adverse attribution phrase governed by the speech frame
contrastive fabrication reading of the speech verb
final accusative false-content noun

words.prose: {{ar:تَقُولَ}} ({{tr:taqūla}}) names the communicative act inside {{ar:لَّن}} ({{tr:lan}}), so the speech is a projected non-occurrence within the speakers' mistaken assumption. The verb is heard before the paired subject {{ar:ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ}} ({{tr:al-insu wa-l-jinnu}}), foregrounding the act before the communities whose reliability was overestimated. The q-w-l field keeps this as accountable assertion laid {{ar:عَلَى ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalā Allāhi}}), not mere vocal sound. A {{ar:تَقَوَّلَ}} ({{tr:taqawwala}}) reading would make fabrication internal to the verb, but the local surface keeps simple saying and lets {{ar:كَذِبًۭا}} ({{tr:kadhiban}}) supply the explicit false-content charge. The broader false-speech pattern is concrete in 3:78 and 6:93, while 72:4 gives the adjacent same-surah speech against Allah and 72:1 places q-w-l inside the surah's repeated audit of reported speech.

topics.headline: speech act lies inside future negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the speech event inside the failed prediction rather than treating it as a completed report.
topics.reason: QAC parses the verb as imperfect subjunctive, and attachment evidence has it governed by lan.

topics.headline: act precedes the named agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first hears the forbidden communicative act, then discovers that the imagined incapable agents are both visible and hidden classes.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies both later nouns as coordinated subjects, while QAC notes that the singular verb can govern the coordinated collective subject.

topics.headline: qawl is assertion with content
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the issue is not noise or casual talk but a claim with content and responsibility.
topics.reason: V4 and contextual evidence support the q-w-l range as formulated saying and report, and the local frame supplies content and an attribution target.

topics.headline: variant makes fabrication verbal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can see how a fabrication reading would intensify the accusation, while the local surface still lets the final falsehood noun carry the explicit truth-failure label.
topics.reason: The variant is valid contrastive evidence, but the aligned local word is parsed as Form I saying and is followed by the explicit accusative falsehood.

topics.headline: false attribution is a known speech crime
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that 72:5 underestimates a recognized pattern of false speech against Allah, with 3:78, 6:93, and 72:4 giving concrete anchors.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows connect q-w-l with false attribution to Allah at 3:78, 6:93, and adjacent 72:4 while preserving the local predicate.

words.gloss_range: humankind, visible humans, the human class; locally a definite nominative class subject paired with jinn
words.root_gloss_range: familiarity, sociability, visibility, and a debated relation to forgetfulness; locally visible humanity as a class, not an isolated crowd

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: coordinated hidden class paired with the human subject

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْإِنسُ}} ({{tr:al-insu}}) arrives after the verb as a definite nominative class subject, so the failed expectation concerns humanity as a visible class rather than a few individuals. Its ʾ-n-s field makes familiar social visibility part of the payoff: the speakers overestimated the reliability of the known human sphere. The etymological dispute with forgetfulness can color that reliability question, but the local noun remains the human class. Its placement before {{ar:ٱلْجِنُّ}} ({{tr:al-jinnu}}) makes humans the first named test case even inside a jinn-reported surah; the same visible-hidden pair continues in 72:6 and also appears in the speech challenge of 17:88.

topics.headline: humanity is a class subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the claim ranges over the human class as a subject pole, not merely over scattered individuals.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the noun as definite, nominative, and the explicit subject of the speech verb; contextual evidence supports generic human reference.

topics.headline: familiar visibility pressures reliability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that visible social familiarity itself becomes part of the failed trust in speech reliability.
topics.reason: The familiarity and sociability field survives as semantic pressure, while the local form and syntax select the human class rather than making forgetfulness the lexical sense.

topics.headline: human first opens the paired horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears humans named first, then the jinn, so the assumption expands from the visible social world into a total visible-hidden speaker horizon.
topics.reason: The rows supply concrete parallels at 17:88, 72:6, and the local word order; attachment evidence confirms the coordinated pair under one predicate.

words.gloss_range: and; locally a coordinator adding the jinn class to the same negated predicate already opened with humans

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: coordinated hidden class added by the conjunction
preceding human class joined to the jinn by the conjunction

words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) binds {{ar:ٱلْجِنُّ}} ({{tr:al-jinnu}}) to {{ar:ٱلْإِنسُ}} ({{tr:al-insu}}) under the same negated speech predicate. Its payoff is not just additive grammar; it widens the failed assumption in real time from the familiar visible class to the concealed class, making both share the imagined impossibility.

topics.headline: conjunction totalizes the subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the assumption widen from human society to jinn, with both classes sharing one negated false-speech expectation.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the following jinn noun as coordinated with the human noun under the same verb; contextual evidence shows the pair is a strong collocational relation for this jinn form.

words.gloss_range: the jinn, hidden beings, the concealed class; locally a definite nominative class subject coordinated with humans
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealment, hiddenness, protection, and covered mind in other derivatives; locally hidden beings as accountable agents, not deranged individuals

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: coordinated visible human class paired with the jinn

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْجِنُّ}} ({{tr:al-jinnu}}) completes the subject pair as a definite nominative class coordinated with {{ar:ٱلْإِنسُ}} ({{tr:al-insu}}). The j-n-n concealment field matters positively: the hidden class is not exempted by hiddenness but is made a full subject of possible accountable speech. The family may include covered-mind derivatives, yet the local surface selects the concealed beings. Because 72:1 introduces jinn as listeners and reporters, 72:5 turns the surah's own reporting group into part of the judged speaker horizon; the word also completes the visible-hidden pair only after the verb has already been heard.

topics.headline: jinn share the subject role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees hidden beings made full class subjects of the same false-speech possibility as humans.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence parse the noun as definite, nominative, and coordinated with the human subject under the same speech verb.

topics.headline: concealment becomes accountable agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the semantic pressure of hiddenness while keeping the local referent as the concealed class of beings.
topics.reason: The j-n-n covering field supports hiddenness as pressure, but the local noun names the jinn class rather than other derivatives such as covered mind.

topics.headline: narrators enter the judged class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the jinn who report in 72:1 are not outside the critique; 72:5 includes their class among those once misjudged as unable to utter falsehood.
topics.reason: The source rows give a same-surah anchor at 72:1, letting the word function as self-including critique without changing its local subject role.

topics.headline: hidden class completes the horizon
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the subject horizon complete after the speech act has already sounded: act first, then visible and hidden agents.
topics.reason: The local word order places the verb before the coordinated subject pair, with jinn completing the pair after humans.

words.gloss_range: on, upon, against, over; locally adverse attribution governing the divine name after a speech verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: proper divine name governed by the preposition
final falsehood noun naming the charge
prepositional attribution phrase before the final falsehood

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) turns the saying into adverse attribution: the speech is not merely about Allah, but laid against Him as a claim. It governs {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) and attaches to the speech event, while {{ar:كَذِبًۭا}} ({{tr:kadhiban}}) remains the content or charge. The phrase {{ar:عَلَى ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalā Allāhi}}) comes before the final falsehood, so the violated authority is named before the truth failure is disclosed. The same attribution frame links 72:4 and 72:5, with the charge sharpening from overstepping in 72:4 to falsehood here.

topics.headline: preposition lays the claim against Allah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the false speech is framed as an adverse attribution laid against a named authority, not as neutral talk about a topic.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence links the preposition to the speech verb and makes the divine name its governed complement, with translation support warning against neutral spatial reading.

topics.headline: target appears before the final falsehood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader first hears whom the speech violates, then receives the final noun naming the violation as falsehood.
topics.reason: The local order places the prepositional target before the final accusative falsehood.

topics.headline: same frame sharpens the charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the transition from 72:4's overstepping claim to 72:5's explicit falsehood within the same attribution frame.
topics.reason: The boundary row gives a concrete adjacent anchor at 72:4 and the same prepositional frame.

words.gloss_range: Allah, the proper divine name; locally genitive after adverse-attribution preposition and the named target of false speech
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with associated worshiped-authority field and debated derivational background; locally Allah by name, not a generic deity category

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preposition governing the divine name
final accusative falsehood noun following the named target

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is governed by {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), so the lie is directed against the proper divine name inside the attribution frame. The proper-name form fixes the target: the ayah is not speaking only of sacred authority in general, but of Allah by name. The ʾ-l-h worshiped-authority field intensifies the offense, with awe, bewilderment, and exaltation left as background pressure rather than replacing the proper-name function. The name stands before {{ar:كَذِبًۭا}} ({{tr:kadhiban}}), so the authority is identified before the final falsehood. Inter-ayah evidence sharpens the pattern: 6:93 condemns inventing lies against Allah, 72:12 moves the same name from target of false speech to inescapable power, and the surah repeatedly corrects claims about Allah in 72:4, 72:7, 72:12, 72:18, 72:19, 72:22, and 72:23.

topics.headline: proper name fixes the target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the false attribution is fixed to Allah by name, not to a generic divine category.
topics.reason: QAC parses the word as a proper noun in genitive after the preposition, and attachment evidence makes it the target of the speech attribution.

topics.headline: divinity field intensifies offense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader senses why the attribution is grave: it is made against named worshiped authority, while the local grammar still selects the proper name.
topics.reason: The semantic field of deity and worship is relevant pressure, but QAC and local form keep the referent as the proper divine name.

topics.headline: false attribution has concrete anchors
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the shock of 72:5 against a known Quranic pattern of lies against Allah, especially 6:93.
topics.reason: The source rows provide concrete cross-passage anchors and a local qawl-kadhib attribution cluster.

topics.headline: same name moves through correction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 72:5 within a surah sequence where claims about Allah are corrected, and where 72:12 recasts Allah from target of speech to power none can escape.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give same-surah anchors at 72:4, 72:7, 72:12, 72:18, 72:19, 72:22, and 72:23.

topics.headline: authority precedes the charge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the violated authority before the utterance is finally named as falsehood.
topics.reason: The local order places the governed proper name before the final accusative falsehood noun.

words.gloss_range: falsehood, a lie, lying content; locally an accusative masdar specifying the false content or internal measure of the speech act
words.root_gloss_range: falsehood contrary to truth, lying, accusing of lying, and other secondary idioms; locally truth-value failure in speech laid against Allah

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: adverse attribution frame intensifying the falsehood
speech verb whose content is specified by the final accusative

words.prose: {{ar:كَذِبًۭا}} ({{tr:kadhiban}}) seals the ayah as the final accusative charge. It can be read as spoken content and as a cognate-like measure of the act, so the speech is specified as falsehood rather than merely described by manner. Its root names a mismatch between claim and reality, intensified by the frame {{ar:عَلَى ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalā Allāhi}}). Because the ayah uses {{ar:تَقُولَ}} ({{tr:taqūla}}) plus {{ar:كَذِبًۭا}} ({{tr:kadhiban}}) rather than a single lying verb, the public act of saying and the truth-value failure are held apart. The final indefinite form broadens the category to any false attribution, while the delayed placement makes falsehood the terminal disclosure. The inter-ayah field is concrete: 3:78 and 6:93 name false speech against Allah, 18:5 and 16:116 warn against saying falsehood, 72:4 moves from one offender's overstepping to 72:5's universal visible-hidden speaker horizon, and the boundary turns external accusation into the speakers' own correction while 72:5 itself links supposition with lie in a marked way.

topics.headline: accusative names what is uttered
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees falsehood as the content or inner measure of the utterance, not merely as an adverbial description of speaking.
topics.reason: QAC parses a gerund/masdar accusative, attachment evidence marks it as the explicit content object, and role profiles show this form often functioning as direct object.

topics.headline: root marks mismatch with truth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the final word name truth-value failure itself, not only excessive or outrageous speech.
topics.reason: V4 evidence supports the central k-dh-b branch as falsehood contrary to truth, with related act, agent, and object derivatives.

topics.headline: speech act and false content are split
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the wording separates the act of saying from the false content, making communicative assertion answerable to truth.
topics.reason: The local syntax has a speech verb with an explicit accusative falsehood noun, and the root-pair rows identify the accountability payoff.

topics.headline: final indefinite broadens and seals
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the charge arrive at the end as a broad category of false attribution, not as one already specified lie or an assigned liar label.
topics.reason: The local noun is an indefinite masdar in final position, and attachment evidence makes it the content object of the speech verb.

topics.headline: false speech field sharpens the confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 72:5's final word inside concrete warning patterns: lies against Allah in 3:78 and 6:93, and saying falsehood in 18:5 and 16:116.
topics.reason: The source rows give explicit inter-ayah anchors and note that k-dh-b with supposition is comparatively marked.

topics.headline: boundary moves from accusation to confession
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees 72:5 transform 72:4's accusation about one offender into the speakers' own correction about both visible and hidden classes.
topics.reason: The boundary rows give the adjacent 72:4 to 72:5 movement from one fool's overstepping speech to a broader confessed assumption about falsehood.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction ظَنَنَّا أَن لَّن joins a prior judgment to the predicted absence of تَقُول ... كَذِبًا.
baseline_models.mechanism: A belief carried as certainty after an indication is retrospectively confessed as failed because the expected absence of false utterance did not hold. The focus ayah therefore stages an epistemic reversal, not merely an accusation.

activation_trace.role: Certainty reached after an indication supplies the high confidence that the confession later overturns.
Articulated utterance makes the failed expectation concern publicly expressible speech.
Falsehood opposed to truth supplies the event whose occurrence breaks the prior certainty.

changed_reading.before: The speakers thought that neither humans nor jinn would lie about Allah.
changed_reading.after: The speakers confess that an indication-based certainty about trustworthy speakers collapsed when false divine attribution became possible.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The sequence تَقُول ... عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا binds saying, divine reference, and falsehood.
baseline_models.mechanism: The saying branch includes speaking what never occurred or attaching words to another. Placed against the worshipped One, the failure is the appropriation of divine authority by manufactured attribution, not generic interpersonal dishonesty.

activation_trace.role: False saying or false attribution supplies the act of attaching an invented claim to an authority.
The worshipped One supplies the uniquely consequential authority against whom the attribution is made.
Falsehood in speech or action marks the attributed claim as contrary to truth.

changed_reading.before: Humans and jinn tell a generic lie concerning God.
changed_reading.after: Humans and jinn can manufacture a claim and place it upon divine authority, turning speech into unauthorized attribution.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The inward ظَنَنَّا precedes and evaluates the outward تَقُول, while the whole claim is voiced as a first-person confession.
baseline_models.mechanism: Uncertain supposition can be an unspoken saying in the self, and the false soul branch makes that inner discourse suspect. The first failed speech in the ayah may therefore be the speakers' own reassuring narration about others, even before any external lie is identified.

activation_trace.role: Weak or uncertain supposition supplies the fallible inward judgment being confessed.
An unspoken saying conceived in the self turns ظَنَنَّا into an internal speech event.
The soul named as false supplies a contained possibility of self-deception behind confidence in others.

changed_reading.before: The verse blames unreliable speech located wholly outside the confessing group.
changed_reading.after: The confession also indicts the group's own inner saying: their reassuring assumption was itself an unreliable discourse.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated subjects الْإِنسُ وَالْجِنُّ place visible human presence beside hidden spirit beings under one speech predicate.
baseline_models.mechanism: The paired subjects span perceptible and concealed social domains, while qawl can be circulating public report. The failed trust was therefore system-wide: speech from both visible and hidden channels was treated as mutually credible.

activation_trace.role: Visible human presence supplies the perceptible side of the paired speaker field.
Hidden spirit beings supply the concealed side of the same speaker field.
Circulating talk supplies the medium through which the two domains can form one report ecology.

changed_reading.before: Two creature classes happen to be named as possible liars.
changed_reading.after: The ayah confesses misplaced trust in an entire visible-hidden report ecology through which claims about Allah could circulate.

context_deltas.mechanism: A newly heard, unfamiliar recitation with a concealed divine origin supplies direct evidence, while the immediately preceding saying is marked as foolish and far from truth. This revises the focus confession into a source audit: inherited confidence yields when received speech can be compared with an authenticated disclosure.

activation_trace.role: Divine report or inspiration supplies the newly authenticated origin against which prior claims are tested.
Hearing that becomes understanding and compliance supplies direct reception rather than secondhand reputation.
Recitation supplies the articulated evidence that can be heard and evaluated.
Wonder at an unfamiliar matter marks the evidence as disruptive of settled expectation.
Lightness of mind and deficient restraint classify the earlier speaker as an unreliable authority.
Deviation from truth supplies the diagnosed direction of that speaker's saying.

structural_cues: 72:1 orders concealed imparting, attentive hearing, and reported hearing before the retrospective confession in 72:5.
72:4 places a known speaker and his excessive saying immediately before the former universal confidence of 72:5.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies newly heard recitation and a prior saying labeled foolish and deviant; I infer that comparison with the new source breaks the old confidence. A live alternative is that the sequence reports conversion without making an explicit evidence protocol.

changed_reading.before: The speakers simply discover that their belief about truthful speakers was wrong.
changed_reading.after: Directly heard disclosure audits inherited reports, exposing their former certainty as confidence maintained without source comparison.

context_deltas.mechanism: The visible and hidden groups are not merely parallel speaker classes. Human men seek protection with jinn men, and the relation produces increase and overpowering burden. That patronage circuit gives concealed agents social authority and creates a feedback path through which claims can be trusted, repeated, and intensified.

activation_trace.role: Men on both sides supply matched social actors rather than abstract species.
Visible human presence supplies the dependent party entering the cross-domain relation.
Seeking refuge and protection supplies the asymmetry that grants another speaker authority.
Hidden spirit beings supply the concealed patrons whose claims are difficult to inspect directly.
Increase and growth supply the amplifying result of the relation.
Overwhelming and subjugating pressure supplies the harmful form taken by that amplification.

structural_cues: 72:6 duplicates رِجَال across the human-jinn boundary and connects the parties through يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍ.
The final فَزَادُوهُمْ marks an outcome flowing from the relation rather than merely listing the two groups.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies refuge across the human-jinn boundary followed by increased rahaq; I infer a trust and authority circuit capable of amplifying reports. Rahaq could instead be an outcome of the relation without speech being its transmission mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Humans and jinn independently produce false claims about Allah.
changed_reading.after: False divine attribution can be sustained by a patronage loop in which visible people authorize hidden patrons and the exchange magnifies oppressive excess.

context_deltas.mechanism: The exact ظن ... أن لن pattern recurs around different outcomes. In 72:7 it is shared as a failed supposition; in 72:12 it supports recognition that neither terrestrial maneuver nor flight can escape Allah. The focus ظَنَنَّا is therefore confidence whose reliability must be calibrated by indication and outcome, not assigned one fixed strength.

activation_trace.role: Uncertain supposition supplies the shared mistaken pattern explicitly compared across groups.
Certainty after an indication supplies the contrasting, firmer use of the same judgment root.
Outrunning or escaping pursuit supplies the concrete impossibility now recognized with confidence.
Frightened flight supplies the second failed escape route that stabilizes the later judgment.

structural_cues: 72:7 echoes the focus with ظَنُّوا كَمَا ظَنَنتُمْ أَن لَّن and marks the assumption as shared.
72:12 repeats وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَن لَّن but coordinates two failed escape routes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated syntax and branch senses ranging from supposition to certainty; I infer deliberate epistemic recalibration through changed outcomes. Alternatively, every use may denote strong belief while only the proposition, not confidence level, changes.

changed_reading.before: ظَنَنَّا is a neutral mental verb meaning that the speakers thought something.
changed_reading.after: ظَنَنَّا names a once-confident but untested expectation whose epistemic quality is exposed by what later proves escapable, inescapable, or false.

context_deltas.mechanism: The speaking jinn explicitly partition themselves into sound and other members, diverse paths, those who hand themselves over, and those who deviate. This internal differentiation revises the focus pair الْإِنسُ وَالْجِنُّ: class membership cannot function as a warrant of truthfulness.

activation_trace.role: Soundness opposed to corruption supplies one positive subgroup within the speakers.
Otherness supplies members outside the named sound subgroup without forcing one homogeneous remainder.
Extended paths supply distinct courses along which members proceed.
Diverse paths and parties make the community's internal divisions explicit.
Handing over and relinquishing supplies one community response to the newly heard guidance.
Deviation from the right supplies the opposed community response.

structural_cues: 72:11 repeats مِنَّا ... وَمِنَّا and closes with طَرَائِقَ قِدَدًا.
72:14 again repeats مِنَّا ... وَمِنَّا before contrasting responses.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit intragroup partitions; I infer that these correct the blanket trust implied by treating a whole class as unable to lie. The correction is explicit for the speaking jinn and only analogically extends to humans.

changed_reading.before: The focus makes a factual mistake about two homogeneous species.
changed_reading.after: The focus confesses an epistemic mistake in using broad group identity as a truth credential despite real internal plurality.

context_deltas.mechanism: Listening access is watched, unseen knowledge is selectively disclosed to an accepted messenger, guards are inserted around the route, delivery is completed, and the whole process is comprehensively known and counted. This turns the focus problem into provenance: a claim about Allah is trustworthy through an authorized and guarded transmission path, not because its speaker is human, jinn, or hidden.

activation_trace.role: Auditory reception supplies the access point whose legitimacy is under scrutiny.
Watching and guarding supply enforcement against unlicensed listening.
Delivering a message supplies the speaker's constrained transmission task.
Messenger and message supply the authorized carrier and payload in the chain.
What is concealed from eyes supplies the protected information domain.
Disclosure and emergence supply the controlled transition from hidden knowledge to manifestation.
Acceptance rather than displeasure supplies selective authorization of the messenger.
Inserting one thing into another supplies the placement of guards within the transmission route.
Watching and guarding on the messenger's route supply chain protection at both ends.
Complete enclosure in knowledge and custody supplies end-to-end oversight of delivery.
Exhaustive enumeration supplies an auditable completion condition rather than vague assurance.

structural_cues: 72:9 places present listening beside an already prepared watcher.
72:26-28 forms a chain from hidden knowledge through selective disclosure and guarding to known delivery and exhaustive count.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies restricted listening, selective disclosure, guarded routing, completed delivery, and comprehensive oversight; I infer that these together function as provenance control for divine claims. A live alternative is that the guards protect the mission or messenger without serving as a general truth-authentication model.

changed_reading.before: A claim about Allah is accepted or rejected mainly by judging the class of its speaker.
changed_reading.after: A divine claim requires guarded provenance from authorized disclosure through completed delivery; hidden-source prestige and group identity do not authenticate it.

context_deltas.mechanism: Firewood is gathered fuel and also carries a tale-bearing branch; a crowd becomes material piled layer upon layer, and fire appears as the consequence. These images activate a material-social reading in which false attribution is not an inert sentence but speech gathered, layered, and made consequential by circulation.

activation_trace.role: Gathered firewood supplies material that accumulates and becomes fuel.
Carrying firewood as tale-bearing or slander links gathered fuel to harmful speech circulation.
Material pressed layer upon layer supplies the social accumulation of repeated speech.
Kindled fire supplies the consequence fed by the accumulated material.

structural_cues: 72:15 makes the deviating group firewood, 72:19 depicts a piled multitude, and 72:23 names fire.
The focus itself couples saying with falsehood, keeping the material analogy anchored in speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies firewood with a tale-bearing branch, piled matter, and kindled fire; I infer a rhetorical arrow from circulating false speech to accumulated consequence. The three images may instead describe punishment and crowd behavior independently of a speech mechanism.

changed_reading.before: A lie about Allah is a discrete proposition uttered once.
changed_reading.after: False attribution has a material social afterlife: repeated circulation gathers and layers it into fuel for consequence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant ق و ل to ق ل ل mapping and must not replace the grammatical sense of تَقُول. It remains packet-anchored because the focus inventory explicitly supplies fewness and 72:24 repeats that same mapped branch beside number. Downstream prose should present it only as a metalinguistic frequency resonance around the categorical لَن, not as a translation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The categorical expectation أَن لَّن تَقُول is activated by the non-dominant fewness branch attached to focus تَقُول.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant fewness branch reframes categorical impossibility as an unmeasured judgment that false attribution is effectively too scarce to occur.
Explicit fewness repeats the same mapped branch when comparative scarcity finally becomes an object of knowledge.
Counting the numbered supplies the measurement that the earlier absolute expectation lacked.

changed_reading.before: The speakers make only a categorical claim that false divine speech will never occur.
changed_reading.after: As a secondary resonance, their categorical never conceals an unmeasured frequency judgment: they treated such false attribution as too rare to count until actual number became knowable.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because a material expectation-failure branch of ك ذ ب is transferred into a speech setting. It remains valid as an exploratory layer because the focus names كَذِبًا and the later sequence joins promised future, sight, knowledge, and reaching the endpoint. Downstream prose should retain ordinary intentional falsehood as primary and qualify this only as an outcome-tested dimension of a claim.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: كَذِبًا carries a branch in which an expected supply disappears or does not last.

activation_trace.role: Milk failing to last as expected supplies a material image for a claim that does not hold up.
Seeing by eye or insight supplies the eventual observation against which the claim is tested.
A promising sign from which a future state is expected supplies the expectation awaiting fulfillment.
Disclosure to the knower supplies the epistemic result once the promised matter is seen.
Reaching the endpoint supplies fulfillment of the transmission charge rather than mere verbal assertion.

changed_reading.before: كَذِبًا denotes only a speaker's intentional assertion of what is untrue.
changed_reading.after: As a contained secondary layer, false speech is also a claim that fails its expected duration or destination when later sight and completed delivery test it.

strongest_changes: Newly heard disclosure turns the failed assumption into a comparison between inherited report and authenticated reception.
Human refuge with jinn changes two speaker classes into an asymmetric feedback network that can amplify harmful claims.
Repeated ظن ... أن لن syntax and explicit intragroup plurality expose both confidence calibration and category-based trust as problems.
Guarded access, selective disclosure, messenger routing, delivery, and exhaustive oversight recast truth as a provenance question.
summary.what_was_special: The focus-only branches already distinguished failed certainty, unauthorized attribution, inner self-deception, and a visible-hidden report field. Context then supplied a social amplification circuit and an unusually explicit guarded transmission architecture; the split ق و ل to ق ل ل mapping also produced a contained frequency resonance at 72:24.
remaining_uncertainties: The refuge-to-rahaq relation clearly amplifies harm, but the packet does not state that speech is the medium of that amplification.
The guarded route may authenticate message provenance, protect the messenger, or do both.
The material fulfillment and frequency readings are branch-supported resonances, not replacements for the ordinary senses of كذب and تقول.
The repeated ظن forms permit confidence calibration, but their exact degree of certainty remains locally variable.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A failed trust in the speech of both visible and hidden communities.** `ظننا` activates ظ ن ن B003, uncertain supposition, alongside B001, certainty after an indication; `تقول` activates ق و ل B001/B005, utterance and false attribution; `الإنس` activates ء ن س B001, visible human presence; `الجن` activates ج ن ن B001/B005, concealed beings; and `كذبا` activates ك ذ ب B001, falsehood against truth. Pairing humans and jinn exhausts the visible/hidden social field. The abductive move is that the hearers had mistaken a socially comprehensive expectation for reliable evidence. The ayah reads as an epistemic confession: confidence in speakers, across both domains, had screened off the possibility of false attribution.

2. **Supposition corrected by reception rather than by another supposition.** The repeated speech vocabulary of 72:4-5 is opposed structurally to `استمع/سمعنا` in 72:1 and the immediate movement to faith in 72:2. The packet supplies the contrast between inherited saying and newly heard recitation; the inferred arrow is that tested reception displaces untested expectation. `ظننا` therefore reads retrospectively as a vulnerable prior model, not simply as a belief they once happened to hold.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The repeated `ظن` in 72:7 and explicit `لا ندري` in 72:10 reveal that the surprise is methodological: shared confidence does not become knowledge. Controlled disclosure in 72:26 supplies the final correction.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A certainty is reclassified as an unreliable inference.** Fixed `ظ ن ن` B001 is certainty after an indication, whereas B003 is uncertain supposition from a weak indication and B006 an affair whose outcome cannot be trusted. The immediate confession follows evidence that their own fool spoke extravagantly (72:4), and the later sequence moves from discovering altered sky access (72:8-9) to `لَا نَدْرِىٓ` (72:10). The packet supplies their former confidence, counterevidence, and explicit present uncertainty; I infer that retrospective confession downgrades what felt like knowledge into poorly grounded expectation. `ظَنَنَّا` reads as an epistemic error report, not neutral belief.

2. **Visibility and concealment no longer predict truthfulness.** Fixed `ء ن س` B001 frames humans as visible presence over against the hidden beings of `ج ن ن` B005. The two are coordinated as a single subject of `تَقُولَ`, and 72:6-7 shows beliefs and practices circulating between those populations. The packet supplies the visible/hidden contrast and shared social transmission; I infer that false attribution crosses the perceptual boundary and therefore cannot be screened by the speaker's kind. `ٱلْإِنسُ وَٱلْجِنُّ` reads as an exhaustive failure of source-class trust.

3. **Falsehood is failure of a relay.** Fixed `ق و ل` B005 marks false saying or attribution and fixed `ك ذ ب` B001 falsehood against truth; this pair contrasts with the quoted relay of `أُوحِىَ` -> `قُلْ` -> `ٱسْتَمَعَ` -> `فَقَالُوا` in 72:1. The packet supplies two transmission chains, one explicitly sourced and one speech `على الله`; I infer that source attachment is what distinguishes faithful relaying from counterfeit relaying. The verse therefore reads as a newly learned protocol for evaluating claims made in God's name.

4. **Their assumption itself enabled misplaced refuge.** The next ayah reports humans seeking refuge in jinn, and 72:7 links the two groups through parallel `ظَنُّوا ... ظَنَنتُمْ`. The packet supplies the fixed assumption, a dependency arrangement, and shared supposition; I infer the arrow that presumed truthfulness made the hidden patrons seem reliable enough to approach. `ظَنَنَّا` consequently becomes a causal admission: an unchecked epistemic premise helped sustain the harmful social practice.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 72:25 repeats `إِنْ أَدْرِىٓ`, converting the early confession into a positive discipline: uncertainty is stated under command rather than covered by `ظ ن ن` B001 confidence. Then 72:26-28 locate hidden knowledge at its source and show authorized disclosure being guarded and counted. Those later ayat sharpen the fixed contrast between counterfeit `ق و ل` B005 and a relay that openly marks what its carrier does not know.

baseline.text: Biz, insanların ve cinlerin Allah hakkında asla yalan söylemeyeceğini sanmıştık.

findings.text: Daha önce kesinlik gibi yaşanan kanaat, karşı kanıtla birlikte zayıf işaretlere dayanan ve sonucuna güvenilemeyen bir varsayım olarak yeniden sınıflandırılır.
Allah adına söylenen bir sözün doğruluğunu konuşanın insan veya cin oluşu değil, sözün kaynağına sadık bir aktarım zincirine bağlılığı belirler.
Konuşanlara duyulan denetlenmemiş güven, 72:6'daki zararlı sığınma düzenini mümkün kılan bir ön kabul olarak görünür.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1: Concealed Dispatch Becomes Epistemic Commitment
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A message moves through controlled stages from hidden transmission to audible form, understanding, and committed response; failure occurs when speech detaches from that chain.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The lexical network treats revelation less as a static text than as a custody chain whose successive operations can be contrasted with the uncontrolled manufacture and circulation of claims.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Speech detaches from evidence and becomes injurious attribution
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Unstable judgment produces excessive or deviant speech, which circulates as hearsay and finally attributes to another words or realities that were never established.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: lightness and agitation (`quranic:root_000717:B001/m01`); deficient judgment (`quranic:root_000717:B002/m01`); declaring a person or view foolish (`quranic:root_000717:B004/m01`); excessive distance beyond a limit (`quranic:root_000795:B001/m01`); deviation from truth in judgment (`quranic:root_000795:B002/m01`); fabricated attribution (`quranic:root_001272:B005/m01`); circulating talk (`quranic:root_001272:B007/m01`); an unvoiced proposition in the mind (`quranic:root_001272:B012/m01`); a proposition hardened into doctrine (`quranic:root_001272:B013/m01`); falsehood opposed to truth (`quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`); charging another with falsehood (`quranic:root_001290:B002/m01`); deceptive appearance (`quranic:root_001290:B009/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The operation is not simply "bad speech." Mental lightness destabilizes judgment; distance and lateral deviation remove a claim from the truth; private formulation then becomes public circulation and false attribution. The deceptive cloth that misstates its own condition gives the process a material endpoint: an utterance can present a patterned surface that does not correspond to what it covers.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Assumption is forced back into acknowledged uncertainty
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Strong belief, weak surmise, suspicion, and unreliable expectation are distinguished until the speakers explicitly admit that another's intended outcome remains unknown.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: conviction inferred from an indicator (`quranic:root_000969:B001/m01`); weak surmise (`quranic:root_000969:B003/m01`); accusation and suspicion (`quranic:root_000969:B004/m01`); habitual mistrust (`quranic:root_000969:B005/m01`); an outcome that cannot be relied upon (`quranic:root_000969:B006/m01`); knowledge and making known (`quranic:root_000473:B001/m01`); intention and volition (`quranic:root_000610:B001/m01`); evil or harmful outcome (`quranic:root_000787:B001/m01`); rectifying direction (`quranic:root_000565:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The same root can name conviction, conjecture, accusation, or an expectation whose end is insecure. The scene therefore sorts epistemic states rather than treating all belief alike. At 72:10 the sorting terminates in a disciplined admission: the observed closure of the sky does not disclose whether harm or rectification is intended.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1: Refuge Brokerage Reverses into Encroachment
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A protection relation should place a vulnerable party within another's shelter, but the human-jinn arrangement reverses the roles and enlarges the very pressure it was meant to contain.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Refuge appears as a social contract, a physical enclosure, and an occult appliance; every form is vulnerable to capture by the broker who claims to provide it.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Visible and hidden collectives enter a protection relation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Human clients approach hidden parties represented as socially legible men, and ask those parties to function as protectors.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: visible humanity opposed to wild hiddenness (`quranic:root_000059:B001/m01`); familiarity that removes estrangement (`quranic:root_000059:B003/m01`); close companion or confidant (`quranic:root_000059:B006/m01`); concealment from perception (`quranic:root_000266:B001/m01`); hidden jinn (`quranic:root_000266:B005/m01`); a massed hidden community (`quranic:root_000266:B013/m01`); adult male social standing (`quranic:root_000546:B002/m01`); flight to a protector (`quranic:root_001059:B001/m01`).
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The encounter crosses the visible-hidden divide but preserves an ordinary social grammar: clients, recognized male brokers, and a request for protection. The human root contributes familiarity and companionship, while the jinn root contributes concealment and a hidden collective. The result is not an abstract superstition but a failed patronage arrangement between two represented communities.

concept_map.definition: Varlığı, içeriği, doğruluğu veya sonucu bilinmediği için güvenilemeyen şeydir. Bu nitelik suyu belirsiz kuyuya, ödenmesi belirsiz alacağa, güvenilmeyen bilgiye ve sonu kestirilemeyen işe uygulanır.

Ödenip ödenmeyeceği bilinmeyen alacak bu niteliğin belirli bir uygulamasıdır.
Güven vermeyen bilgi ve sonucu kestirilemeyen iş de aynı nitelikle anlatılır.

root_profile.summary: Anlam ailesinin merkezinde, bir belirtiye dayanarak kesin bilgi ile zayıf sanı arasında değişen zihinsel değerlendirme bulunur; buradan bir şeyin beklendiği yer, suçlama, başkası hakkında kötü düşünme ve sonucu güven vermeyen şey anlamları ayrışır. Ayrıca düşmanlık eden kişi, güçsüzlük ya da yük kaldırabilme niteliği ve çocuk beklenen saygın kadın gibi sözlüksel olarak uzak dallar vardır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalı sesle ortaya çıkarılan söz ve harflerden kurulu sözlü ifade olarak verir. Geçici çerçeve aynı çekirdeği taşıyor; dil organı, hükümdar unvanı ve mecazi yan kullanımlar bu dalın dışında kalır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal çıplak söz söyleme ve söylenmiş söz çekirdeğidir; organ, unvan, söylenti ve mecazlar ayrı dallardır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Mekanik kapsam bare olduğu için tanım çıplak söyleme ve sözlü ifade anlamıyla sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir düşünceyi veya sözü sesli biçimde dışa vurma ve böyle dışa vurulmuş harfli sözlü ifade anlamıdır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek işlem, sözü sesli olarak dışa çıkarmaktır.
Söylenen şey tek söz, cümle, şiir veya konuşma ölçeğinde olabilir.
Ad biçimleri aynı söylenmiş söz alanında toplanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, sözü sesle dışa çıkarılan ve harflerden oluşan sözlü ifade çekirdeğinde toplar; ad biçimleri de aynı alana bağlıdır.

error_profile.preserves: Sesle dışa vurma ve sözlü ifade çekirdeğini korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Fiil bağlamında kişinin sözü sesli olarak ortaya koymasını karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Fiilsel söyleme işlemini korur.

error_profile.preserves: Söylenmiş ifade sonucunu korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi ilgili biçimi doğrudan konuşma organı olan dil diye açıklar. Geçici çerçeve bu organ anlamını doğru taşır ve söylenmiş söz ya da söz sahibi anlamlarını bu dalın dışında bırakır.

facets.statement: Çekirdek anlam, konuşmayı sağlayan bedensel organdır.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, sesle söze dökme çekirdeğinden konuşma organı, konuşkan kişi, eski unvan, yalan isnat, söylenti, müzakere, hüküm dayatma, iç söz, görüş benimseme, sözsüz belirtme, içten önemseme, teknik tanım ve içe doğan anlam gibi ayrı dallara yayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi azlığı çokluğun karşıtı olarak verir; ayrıca yoksulluk, düşüklük, bir şeyi az görme ve belirli yapılarda yokluğa ya da seyrekliğe yaklaşan kullanımları açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol yalnızca sayı ve miktar azlığını ve buna bağlı kullanımları kapsar; yükseklik, kap, taşıma ve titreme anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Temel azlık anlamı ile yoksullaşma ve az görme gibi türemiş biçimler birlikte bulunur; yokluk ve seyrekleşme anlamları ise yalnızca belirtilen yapılara bağlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin sayı, miktar ya da ölçü bakımından çok olmayışını bildirir. Bundan yoksulluk ve düşüklük, bir şeyi az sayma veya az gösterme ve belirli yapılarda hiçlik ya da seyrek gerçekleşme anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Bir varlığın sayı, miktar veya ölçü bakımından çok olmayışıdır.
Azlık, kişinin yoksullaşması veya toplum içinde düşük ve değersiz görülmesi sonucuna uzanabilir.
Bir şeyi gerçekte ya da değerlendiren kişinin gözünde az sayma ve az gösterme anlamını taşır.
Belirli olumsuzluk ve sıklık yapılarında hiç yokluğu veya bir eylemin pek seyrek gerçekleşmesini anlatır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar azlığın temel sayı ve miktar karşıtlığında birleşir; yoksulluk ve düşüklük, az sayma ve bazı yapılarda yokluğa yaklaşan kullanım bu çekirdeğin düzenli uzantılarıdır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Sayı, miktar veya ölçünün çok olmayışını bildiren temel anlam için uygundur.

branches.what_is_ar: القليل والقِلَّة ضد الكثرة، ويدخل فيه الافتقار والذلة، وتقليل الشيء في العين، واستقلاله، واستعمال القليل للنفي أو للندرة

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyin en üstünü veya başını çekirdek anlam olarak verir; dağın yuvarlak üst bölümü, insan başı ve kılıcın başındaki topuz bu çekirdeğin açık uzmanlaşmalarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol uzamsal başı ve en üst parçayı bildirir; sayısal azlık ya da büyük kap anlamını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel baş ve en üst bölüm anlamı ile dağ tepesi, insan başı ve kılıç topuzu gibi yapıya bağlı uzmanlaşmalar ayrı tutulur.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyin başını veya en üst bölümünü bildirir. Dağın üstteki yuvarlak parçası, insan başı ve kılıcın sap ucundaki topuz bu uzamsal çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin veya oluşumun başı ya da en üstte bulunan bölümüdür.
Dağın en üstünde yer alan, kimi tanımda yuvarlak biçimli bölümünü adlandırır.
İnsan başı ile kılıcın sap ucundaki başlık veya topuz da aynı üst ve baş kavramıyla adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir şeyin başı ve en üst bölümü üzerinde birleşir; dağ tepesi temel örnektir, insan başı ile kılıç topuzu da aynı biçimsel ve uzamsal çizgide yer alır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi büyük bir küp veya iri kap anlamında birleşir; iki kaplık ölçü ve belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler de aynı kap anlamını somutlaştırır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol büyük bir kap türünü ve onun ölçü değerini kapsar; nicelik azlığı veya dağ tepesi anlamını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Büyük küp anlamı çekirdektir; belirli bir bölgeye bağlanan kap adı ile iki kaplık ölçü yalnızca kendi yapılardaki uzmanlaşmalardır.

concept_map.definition: Büyük bir küpü veya küpe benzeyen iri kabı bildirir. Belirli bir bölgenin iri küpleri ve iki böyle kabın aldığı miktar bu kap anlamına bağlı özel kullanımlardır.

facets.statement: Küpe benzeyen, özellikle sıvı taşımaya veya saklamaya elverişli büyük bir kaptır.
Belirli bir bölgeyle anılan iri küpler veya büyük toprak kaplar bu adın tanınmış bir türünü oluşturur.
İki büyük kap, bu iki kabın kendisini veya onların aldığı sıvı miktarını bildiren bir ölçü değeri kazanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar iri bir küp veya büyük kap üzerinde birleşir; tanınmış bölgesel kaplar büyüklüğü örnekler, iki kaplık kullanım ise nesne adını kapasite ölçüsüne taşır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi yükü taşıma veya taşıyabilme ile öznenin yükselip harekete geçmesini aynı kolda açıkça toplar; kuşun uçuşa kalkması, göğün yükselmesi ve yolcuların yüklenip ayrılması ayrı katılımcı gerçekleşmeleridir.

concept_map.definition: Bir yükü kaldırıp taşıyabilmeyi veya üstlenmeyi ve bir öznenin yükselerek harekete geçmesini bildirir. İkinci çizgi kuşun uçuşa kalkmasını, göğün yükselmesini ve yolcuların yüklenip yola koyulmasını kapsar.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi kaldıracak gücü bulmak, onu taşımak veya yük olarak üstlenmektir.
Bir öznenin aşağıdaki konumundan yükselmesi veya kuş gibi harekete ve uçuşa başlamasıdır.
Yolcuların yüklerini alıp bulundukları yerden ayrılarak yolculuğa başlamasıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar bir yükü kaldırıp taşıma ile yukarı kalkarak harekete geçme çizgilerini bir araya getirir; kuş, gök, bulut ve yolcu örnekleri katılımcıya göre bu iki çizgiyi somutlaştırır.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu kol insanda korku veya öfkeyle beliren titremeyle sınırlıdır; nesnelerin genel sallanma ve yerinde duramama hali ayrı koldadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Duygudan doğan titreme temel addır; kişiyi titremenin tutması ve öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi yalnızca ilgili yapılara bağlı anlatımlardır.

concept_map.definition: Bir insanın korku veya öfke yüzünden titremesi, ürpermesi ya da bedensel olarak silkelenmesidir. Durum, kişiyi bir titreme nöbetinin tutması veya öfkenin titremeyle dışa vurulması biçiminde anlatılabilir.

facets.statement: İnsan bedeninde beliren titreme, ürperti veya istemsiz silkiniş halidir.
Titremenin belirleyici nedeni korku ya da öfkedir.
Belirli yapılarda titremenin kişiyi tutması veya kişinin öfkeden titrer hale gelmesi anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar insandaki titreme ve silkinişte birleşir; korku ile öfke başlıca nedenlerdir ve durum hem kişiyi tutan bir nöbet hem öfkenin bedensel belirtisi olarak anlatılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi hareket ettirip sallandırma, nesnenin bulunduğu yerde kararlı duramaması ve hareketin çıkardığı sesi birlikte verir; bunlar tek bir fiziksel hareket olayının neden, sonuç ve işitsel yönleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesneyi hareket ettirip onun yerinden oynamasına ve sarsılmasına neden olmaktır.

Sallanma ve yer değiştirme sırasında çıkan ses, hareket olayının işitsel belirtisi olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanımlar dışarıdan hareket ettirme ile nesnenin kararsızca sallanıp yerinde duramaması üzerinde birleşir; hareketin sesi bu fiziksel olayın ayrılmaz işitsel belirtisi olarak eklenir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısındaki insan türünü, bu türün topluluğunu ve tek bir üyesini birlikte gösterir. Görünür olma açıklaması adlandırma gerekçesidir; insan olmanın kurucu tanımı değildir. Evde kimsenin bulunmadığını bildiren kalıp ise dal çekirdeğine genellenemez ve yalnızca kendi sözcüksel biriminde korunmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, insan türünü ve onun tekil ya da toplu üyelerini kapsar; yakınlık duygusunu, duyusal algıyı ve insana dönük yanı kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak biçimlerdeki insan ve insan topluluğu anlamı dal çekirdeğidir; evde hiç kimse bulunmadığını anlatan kalıp ayrı tutulur ve çekirdeğe yeni bir genel anlam katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında yer alan insan türünü, bu türün topluluğunu ya da tek bir üyesini belirtir. İnsanların görünür oluşu, bu adlandırma için aktarılan bir gerekçedir.

facets.statement: İnsan türünü, insanların oluşturduğu topluluğu veya bu türün tek bir üyesini görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfının karşısında adlandırır.
Adlandırmanın insanların duyularla görünür oluşuna bağlanması, anlamın özü değil kökene ilişkin bir açıklamadır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar, dalın insan türünü hem topluluk hem tek kişi olarak gösterebildiğinde ve görünmeyen varlıklar sınıfıyla karşıtlık kurduğunda birleşir. Görünürlük, ortak anlamdan çok adlandırmanın gerekçesi olarak sunulur.

concept_gloss.text: insan türü ve bu türden bir kişi

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi görmeyi temel alır, fakat belirli kullanımlarda işitmeyi, bir belirtiyi anlayıp ayırt etmeyi ve çevreye bakarak birini aramayı da aynı dalda aktarır. Bu yüzden dal genel ve sınırsız bir algı yetisi diye tanımlanamaz; her uzantı kendi bağlamına bağlı tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal duyusal olarak fark etmeyi ve belirtilen bağlamlardaki işitme, sezme ve bakıp araştırma kullanımlarını kapsar; yakınlık ve rahatlık duygusunu kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Görüp fark etme çekirdeği ile ses işitme, olgunluk belirtisini ayırt etme ve çevreye bakıp araştırma kalıpları ayrı tutulur; kalıplardaki kapsam çıplak biçime genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi görüp fark etmeyi anlatır. Belirli kullanımlarda bir sesi işitmeye, bir kimsedeki olgunluk belirtisini ya da kaygı veren bir durumu sezmeye ve çevreye bakarak birinin bulunup bulunmadığını araştırmaya uzanır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyi gözle görerek fark etmeyi veya seçmeyi anlatır.
Belirli bir ses nesnesiyle kullanıldığında o sesi işitmeyi anlatır.
Bir kimsedeki olgunluk belirtisini bilip ayırt etmeyi veya kaygı veren bir durumu duyularla sezmeyi anlatabilir.
Çevreye bakıp dikkatle araştırarak birinin bulunup bulunmadığını anlamaya çalışma kullanımını taşır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarılan anlam alanının merkezi görüp fark etmektir. Aynı ifade ailesi belirli nesne ve yapılarda işitme, bir belirtiyi anlayıp ayırt etme, kaygı veren şeyi sezme ve bakıp araştırma yönlerinde kullanılır; bunlar sınırsız bir genel algı anlamı oluşturmaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kimsedeki olgunluk veya kaygı uyandıran durum gibi bir belirtinin ayırt edildiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Duyusal belirtiden bir durumun varlığını anlayıp ayırt etmeyi korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Çevreyi gözleyip birinin bulunup bulunmadığını anlamaya çalışma kullanımında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Dikkatle bakma ile birini bulmaya yönelik araştırmayı birlikte korur.

çevreye bakıp birinin olup olmadığını araştırmak

error_profile.preserves: Bir kişi veya şeye yönelen deneyim fikrini çok genel biçimde korur.
error_profile.loses: Görme, işitme, belirtiyi sezme ve çevreye bakıp araştırma işlemlerini siler.
error_profile.adds: Zamanla gelişen yakınlık ve yabancılığın kalkması anlamını ekler.
error_profile.collision: Yakınlık ve rahatlık bildiren ayrı dalla karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, görmenin yanında belirli yapılarda işitme, belirti sezme ve çevreyi araştırma uzantılarını taşır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal göz organını, görme duyusunu ve göz açıp dikkatle bakma eylemini kendi başına kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: fark etme ile gözle görme ayrımı
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir şeyi göz yoluyla görüp seçme alanında örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Yalnız görsel algı bağlamında yakın karşılık olabilirler. Odak dalın işitme ve belirtiyi sezme uzantıları komşuya, komşunun göz organı anlamı da odak dala taşınamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal görmeyi merkez alır ve yalnız belirli söz çevrelerinde işitme, sezme ve araştırmaya uzanır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal herhangi bir duyu aracılığıyla algılama, bilme ve varlığını saptama alanını genel olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: belirli algı kullanımları ile genel duyumsama
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her ikisi de bir şeyin duyular aracılığıyla fark edilmesini anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu daha genel bir duyu alanıdır; odak dalın uzantıları ise kanıtlanan nesne ve yapılara bağlıdır. Bu nedenle genel duyumsama her durumda odak ifadeyle karşılanamaz.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal bir nesneyi görme, işitme veya belirtilerinden sezme eylemini anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal bir kişi ya da şey karşısında yabancılık ve ürkme duymayıp yakınlık hissetmeyi anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: duyusal fark etme ile yakınlık hissetme
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kişi veya şeyle karşılaşma iki anlam alanının ortak başlangıç durumu olabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal algısal saptamayı, komşu dal ise karşılaşma sonrasındaki duygusal rahatlığı bildirir. Algı gerçekleşebilir ama yakınlık doğmayabilir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün aday kartlar değerlendirildi. Görme, genel duyumsama ve yakınlık duygusuyla karışma olasılığı en yüksek üç sınır yayımlandı; diğer adaylar dalı açıklayan ek bir karşıtlık sağlamadı.
branches.branch_image_ar: إيناس الشيء برؤية أو إحساس أو سماع
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه آنس الشيء إذا أبصره أو رآه، وآنس الصوت إذا سمعه، وأحس الفزع أو وجد الشيء في نفسه، والاستئناس بمعنى النظر والتبصر.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل الأنس بمعنى الراحة والمؤالفة ولا الإنس بمعنى البشر إلا بقرينة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: آنست الشيء إذا رأيته وآنسته إذا سمعته (maqayis)؛ آنسته أبصرته وآنست الصوت سمعته وآنست منه رشدا علمته (sihah)؛ آنس من جانب يعني أبصر نارا والاستئناس النظر وأحس بما رابه (tahdhib)؛ فإن آنستم منهم رشدا أي أبصرتم وآنست نارا (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir kişi veya şey karşısında yabancılık ve ürkme duygusunun kalkmasını çekirdek anlam olarak verir. Yakınlık ve sevinç, rahatlık veren kişi ya da şey ve insana alışık saldırgan olmayan hayvan kullanımları bu çekirdekten bağımlı biçimde açıklanabilir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal duygusal yakınlık, rahatlık ve bunları sağlayan varlıkları kapsar; insan türünün adı, duyusal fark etme ve insana bakan yan anlamları dışarıda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yabancılık duymama çekirdeği ile rahatlık veren kişi veya şey ve insana alışık hayvan gibi özelleşmiş biçimler ayrı katmanlarda tutulur; özel biçimler bütün dalı tanımlamaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişi ya da şey karşısında yabancılık, ürkme veya kaçınma duymayıp yakınlık, rahatlık ve sevinç hissetmeyi anlatır. Bu duyguyu veren kişi veya şeye ve insana alışık, saldırgan olmayan hayvana da aktarılır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi ya da şey karşısında yabancılık ve ürkme duygusunun kalkıp yakınlık, rahatlık veya sevinç oluşmasını anlatır.
Kişiye arkadaşlık ederek veya yanında bulunarak yabancılık duygusunu gideren kişi ya da şeyi adlandırır.
İnsana alışık ve saldırgan olmayan hayvanı, özellikle bu nitelikteki köpeği anlatabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak çekirdek, yabancılık ve kaçınmanın karşıtı olan yakınlık ve rahatlıktır. Bu durum birine alışıp onun yanında sevinmeyi, rahatlık veren kişi veya şeyi ve insana alışık saldırgan olmayan hayvanı kapsayacak biçimde genişler.

concept_gloss.text: yabancılık duymadan yakınlık ve rahatlık hissetme
concept_gloss.applicability: Bir kişi veya şeyin ürkütücü ve yabancı gelmemesi, tersine yakınlık ve iç rahatlığı vermesi anlatıldığında dalın çekirdeğini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Yabancılığın kalkmasıyla oluşan yakınlık ve rahatlık bağını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişi veya şey karşısındaki yabancılık duygusunun kalktığı temel durumda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Alışma sonucunda yabancılığın kalkmasını ve yakınlık oluşmasını korur.

contextual_glosses.text: yanında rahatlık veren kişi veya şey
contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızlığı veya ürkmeyi gideren bir arkadaş, nesne ya da başka bir dayanak adlandırıldığında uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yakınlık ve güven veren kaynağın kişiyle sınırlı olmamasını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: İnsandan kaçmayan ve ısırıp saldırmayan evcil ya da alışkın hayvan için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Hayvanın insana alışıklığını ve saldırgan olmama sınırını birlikte korur.

yakın arkadaş; rahatlık veren kişi veya şey
